done.why: Every route I could find led to a rockfall, a crumbling ledge or a deep stream. The unicorn kept vanishing and the Wizard kept scaring me off, so I judged this first slice explored.

about: A small Zork II-style cave slice. It starts in a barrow, with a lantern and an Elvish sword. You go through a cavern with a ravine, a formal garden with a skittish unicorn, a disorienting carousel room and a marble hall. A meddling Wizard casts spells on you along the way. Many exits are blocked for later.

ending.what: No ending reached. The world kept saying that what lay beyond would have to wait.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared, cast Fear, and I fled to another room.
The fear spell kept bouncing me between rooms and the unicorn vanished before I could examine it.
Most carousel exits are blocked by rockfall.
A pile of jewels in the Carousel Room could not be taken or examined, probably a Wizard illusion.
The lamp and sword descriptions hint that I have been here before.

wished: Examine the unicorn and get the key
Reach the ledge and the rest of the cave
Find out what the small structure in the garden is

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: Charming voice, and it frames this as a sequel.

lines.line: The passage south is choked with a fall of rock not far in. Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait.
lines.why: It marks the edge of the explorable area.

fun.why: Nice atmosphere, but the world is small and the Wizard's random scares got in the way.

engagement.why: I was curious about the unicorn and the key, but I could never get at them.

difficulty.why: Nothing could be solved in the area I reached. The fear spell and the scrambled carousel exits made movement confusing.

interestingness.why: The Zork II feel, the self-aware item text and the Wizard are all interesting.

prose.why: The prose is evocative and funny, especially the item descriptions.
